messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — P1: elevated 5xx rate on /v2/generate across us-east-1. Alerting on-call.
oncall-rotation-bot: Paging Alice Nguyen (primary oncall) — escalation: 5xx spike, customer impact: degraded generation latency and failed requests. :rotating_light:
Alice Nguyen: I’m awake, looking. Any immediate customer-reported issues?
Ben Ortega: We have two support tickets from Acme and Plinth saying generation returns 502 intermittently. Started ~2 minutes ago.
Sanjay Patel: Grafana shows error rate jump from ~0.2% to 12% at 03:24 UTC. Latency also up. Link: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/serve
Alice Nguyen: ok — quick hit list: (1) capture recent logs from edge + runtime for 03:15-03:30 (2) check recent deploys/rollouts (3) check autoscaler events and GPU pool metrics. Who has recent deploy context?
Carol Park: I pushed a small canary of runtime v1.8.3 to canary pool at 03:18 to address a batching regression. Canary rollout was 10% of traffic in us-east-1.
Alice Nguyen: mark that as high-priority hypothesis. Carol — please paste the canary rollout details (images, diff).
Carol Park: image: registry.redwood/realtime:1.8.3-canary
diff summary:
```diff
- batching: enabled
+ batching: enabled
+ kv_cache_prefetch: true
```
Alice Nguyen: thanks. Sanjay — logs please. Share the error snippet from the runtime logs around 03:24.
Sanjay Patel: pasting trimmed logs:
```
2026-03-15T03:23:57Z runtime-xy: ERROR request_id=abc123 status=502 err="kv cache OOM while inserting"
2026-03-15T03:24:02Z runtime-xy: WARN request_id=def456 latency=482ms evicted_kv=1
2026-03-15T03:24:03Z host-proxy: ERROR upstream=runtime-xy status=502 conn=reset
```
Alice Nguyen: kv cache OOM in canary instances — aligns with kv_cache_prefetch change. Hypothesis A: canary config introduced prefetching that increases KV memory usage causing OOMs and 502s. Hypothesis B: unrelated autoscaler flapping causing overload. We should test A first since canary rollouts overlap with spike.
Ben Ortega: I can temporarily route canary traffic back to baseline. Plan: revert canary to 0% for us-east-1 and watch error-rate. Who will own the revert?
Carol Park: I can roll back the canary. Doing a scoped rollback to revert the config flag only. Command I’ll run:
```bash
rctl rollout update --service realtime --region us-east-1 --image registry.redwood/realtime:1.8.2 --selector canary
```
Alice Nguyen: Carol — execute and report. Also capture before/after autoscaler events: `kubectl get hpa -n realtime -w` and `redis-cli info` for KV pool.
Carol Park: executing now. 03:28:10 — starting rollback.
Mike Torres: I'll monitor ingress and proxy logs and keep support notified. Putting a short post in #support: "Investigating 502s on /v2/generate; possible canary rollback in progress." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sanjay Patel: observing node-level memory on canary instances — memory usage jump prior to OOM. Suggest we also temporarily disable prefetch flag if rollback takes time.
Alice Nguyen: Good. Two parallel mitigations: (1) rollback (Carol) (2) if rollback delayed, apply runtime flag disable on canary configmap (Ben) with config patch. Assign owners: rollback=Carol, flag-patch=Ben, monitor=Mike, logs/timeline=Sanjay, incident lead=Alice.
Carol Park: rollback finished at 03:31:04. Canary image now 1.8.2. Verifying pods cycling.
Sanjay Patel: immediate drop in 502s to 1.1% at 03:33 per Grafana. Latency normalizing. Looks promising.
Alice Nguyen: Great. Hold for 10m to confirm stabilization. Meanwhile we need to build an in-thread timeline and collect artifacts for post-incident RCA.
Ben Ortega: Adding timeline notes:
- 03:18 canary rollout realtime:1.8.3-canary (kv_cache_prefetch: true)
- 03:23 metric spike begins
- 03:24 runtime logs show KV cache OOMs on canary
- 03:28 rollback initiated
- 03:31 rollback complete
- 03:33 error rate decreases
Eve Li: I'll export logs and attach to the incident board (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0315-01). Files: runtime-canary-logs-03-15.tar.gz, ingress-proxy-03-15.tar.gz
Alice Nguyen: Good. For the RCA and hypothesis tracking we should maintain a single canonical list. I'll create the hypothesis matrix here in-thread. Use short labels.
- H1 (canary change): kv_cache_prefetch increased memory -> OOM -> 502s. Evidence: logs show OOMs on canary, timing aligns. Repro steps: enable prefetch on a small scale and run a heavy prompt workload.
- H2 (autoscaler): sudden traffic burst exceeded baseline capacity; autoscaler reacted slowly. Evidence: autoscaler events show scale-up after spike. Counter-evidence: OOMs only on canary pods.
- H3 (network): upstream connection resets from host-proxy due to circuit-breaker misconfig. Evidence: `conn=reset` in proxy logs but preceded by OOM in runtime.
Alice Nguyen: Next actions for postmortem:
- Carol to run targeted repro of H1 with KV mem profiling (owner: Carol)
- SRE (Sanjay) to analyze autoscaler timing and propose safety thresholds (owner: Sanjay)
- Ben to review rollout gating for config flags (owner: Ben)
- Mike to confirm customer impact window and update support notes (owner: Mike)
- Eve to upload artifacts and create timeline doc (owner: Eve)
Everyone, please update the incident board checklist.
Carol Park: I'll do repro today: plan to run a 5-minute high-concurrency job with kv cache prefetch enabled and capture heap/kv metrics. ETA 2 hours.
Ben Ortega: I'll open a ticket to require config-flag canaries to run in isolated pools by default. ETA: draft by EOD.
Sanjay Patel: Autoscaler tuning: propose minReplicas=3 for realtime pool; I'll run simulations and post results.
Mike Torres: Support update posted. Customer window: 03:23-03:33 UTC. Notified Acme and Plinth with mitigation summary.
Alice Nguyen: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open. If we have a follow-up action that requires immediate re-mitigation, ping me. Otherwise we'll transition to a formal RCA doc in #postmortems when artifacts are ready. :white_check_mark:
Carol Park: quick note — we saw a single runtime pod in canary crashloop before OOMs spread; I'll include the pod dump in artifacts.
Eve Li: attaching S3 artifact path in incident board: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0315-01/artifacts
Alice Nguyen: Closing live mitigation. Last check in 5m. Thanks all. :bow:
Mike Torres: 03:38 final check — metrics stable, marking incident as mitigated in the incident tool.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status=mitigated severity=P1 mitigated_by=rollback at 03:38 UTC. Postmortem scheduled.
Alice Nguyen: I’ll own the postmortem writeup. Will include hypothesis matrix, repro steps, and action items. Target: 2026-03-17 12:00 UTC.
